answers.reply: The node 7877e099-7c1b-4496-8be7-43264794aea4 returns a list, and a Vega-Lite node takes only a DataFrame or a GeoDataFrame, so the plan does not feed the list to the chart. A Python node, Numbers as a table, turns the list into a DataFrame first, and the new Vega-Lite node receives exactly one data edge, from that node.

answers.source: packages/curio.builtin@1/manifest.json's ports: a Vega-Lite node (vis-vega) takes a DATAFRAME or a GEODATAFRAME, a Python node (data-transformation, computation-analysis) takes and returns more; a GeoTIFF dataset read as a raster (skills/node-functions/SKILL.md's curio_load_data, as docs/examples/dataflows/quad-cities-flood-vulnerability.json's depth loaders read data.scout.flood-depth-2050-2080-no-nbs) and its cells read into a table in Python, as that example's node 34326814-c132-4eb4-9d73-268368968592 reads them (depth.read(1, masked=True))
answers.reply: A Vega-Lite node takes only a DataFrame or a GeoDataFrame, so no edge carries the raster itself into the chart. The plan loads the raster, then a Python node turns its cells into a table of positions and depths, one row per cell that holds a depth, and that table is the one data edge the Vega-Lite heatmap receives.
